question: After Operation Wuambushu was launched together by the French Minister of the Interior and the Minister for Overseas France1, ‘the Comoros warned that they ‘do not intend to receive’ persons expelled from Mayotte [...]

This threat was carried out on Monday 24 April by the Comorian Minister of the Interior, who announced that he had refused a boat transporting migrants permission to dock, as reported by the Le HuffPost2.

Furthermore, an article published in the online version of La Croix on 9 May 2023 recalled that ‘in 2019, an agreement [had] called on Anjouan to cooperate on immigration in exchange for EUR 150 million in development aid’3.

According to the Outremers360° news site, the French Minister of the Interior had noted the ‘more complicated departure procedures to be put in place for Africans from the Great Lakes region’4, and later announced that he would travel to ‘Burundi, Rwanda, Tanzania and Mozambique’ to ‘negotiate readmission agreements’.

The the EEAS’s page for the Delegation of the European Union to Rwanda indicates that the financial allocations earmarked for the country by the EU for the initial period 2021-2024 are set at EUR 260 million5. While in a factsheet, the EEAS mentions that under the National Indicative Programme of the 11th European Development Fund (2015-2020), the European Union allocated EUR 697 million in grants to Mozambique6.

And lastly, under the International Partnerships section of the European Commission’s website, it is indicated that the EU is supporting the development plans of the Tanzania and Zanzibar through the Global Europe Multiannual Indicative Programme (2021-2027) with a EUR 426 million allocation for the initial period7. Does the Commission intend to adjust this aid to reflect the degree of cooperation on migration?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (20.6.2024) The Commission services and the European External Action Service are currently working on the mid-term review of the programming under the Neighbourhood, Development and International Cooperation Instrument – Global Europe (NDICI-GE). It is in this framework that any adjustment of aid will be considered.

This review process aims at having a more strategic approach to the EU international cooperation. Amongst other things, it will define country allocations for the period 2025-2027. Migration is one of the specific areas for assessment that will be considered for the proposed outcome of the mid-term review of the NDICI-GE programming for the remaining period of the current Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF).
